title: Tenali Raman and the Three Greedy Highwaymen

full_text:
While traveling through the dense Nallamala forest on state business, Tenali Raman’s solitary bullock cart was ambushed by three fierce highwaymen: Bhima, Somu, and Kalu.
They dragged Tenali from the cart, demanding his gold.

Tenali remained completely composed. He looked at the three robbers and sighed:
'Brothers, you have stopped me on the wrong day. I carry only fifteen gold coins in my leather pouch.
However, if you spare my life, I will show you where an enormous treasure is buried: a brass chest containing ten thousand gold dinars, hidden by a merchant beneath the roots of the ancient banyan tree by the river!'

Greed ignited in the highwaymen’s eyes. They marched Tenali to the banyan tree and dug into the earth.
To their amazement, their iron spades struck a real iron chest that Tenali had discovered on an earlier journey!
Inside were hundreds of gleaming ancient silver and copper coins!

The three bandits cheered wildly.
Tenali said: 'Brothers, you have labored hard. It is noon, and you must be starving.
Let one of you run to the village tavern a mile away to buy roast meat and bread, while the other two guard the treasure.'

The youngest bandit, Kalu, volunteered and ran to the village.
As soon as he was gone, Bhima whispered to Somu:
'Why should we divide this treasure into three shares? When Kalu returns with the food, let us strike him down with our cudgels, and split the gold between the two of us!'
Somu agreed with a greedy grin.

Meanwhile, on his way back from the village, Kalu thought to himself:
'Why should I share the treasure with those two brutes? I will buy poison from the apothecary and mix it into the roasted meat! When they eat, they will perish, and the entire hoard will be mine!'

Kalu returned to the banyan tree carrying the poisoned food.
The moment he stepped into the clearing, Bhima and Somu leaped from the brush, striking Kalu down with their heavy cudgels!
Kalu collapsed dead upon the grass.

Laughing at their supposed cleverness, Bhima and Somu sat upon the iron chest and ravenously devoured the roasted meat.
Within ten minutes, the deadly poison took effect: both bandits clutched their stomachs, groaned in agony, and fell lifeless beside their victim!

Tenali Raman stepped out from the shade of the banyan tree, shook his head with sorrowful wisdom, and said:
'Greed digs its own grave, and malice poisons its own cup.'

Tenali loaded the iron chest onto his cart, drove to the nearest town, and surrendered the recovered treasure to the magistrate to build an orphanage, demonstrating that evil inevitably consumes itself.
moral: Thieves who unite through greed are easily divided and defeated by their own mutual suspicion.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "Tenali and the Three Thieves"?
options: Wit and humor triumph over arrogance and power
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
